service_boundary: Represents the Chutes hosting service, not the underlying decentralised network protocol or the open-weight models it serves.
regional_controls: Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than named regions, and no customer control over processing geography is documented.
retention_controls: The terms state that API requests, responses, and application content are not used to train models, and that content is not logged for public inference. Customer-created deployments are noted as running code the operator does not control.
routing: Requests reach a named open-weight model on network capacity; private deployments run on dedicated hardware billed by time.
customization: Customers can deploy their own model code and weights as private endpoints on dedicated hardware.
strengths: Confidential-compute execution is marked on every model in the public catalogue rather than offered as a premium tier.
Capacity comes from a decentralised operator network rather than a single cloud, which changes the concentration risk profile.
The platform's own core is published under a permissive licence, which is uncommon among hosted inference operators.
tradeoffs: The catalogue is open-weight only, so it is not an alternative for reaching proprietary frontier models.
The operating entity is unclear, with no named legal company and a team page listing mostly handles.
A pricing path on the operator's own site returns a not-found body under a success status, which would mislead automated checks.

response_integrity.note: The security-architecture page documents a validator-side check ("cllmv (Chutes Large Language Model Verification): This component integrates with the SGLang inference engine to provide per-token verification hashes.") that binds the model name and revision to output proofs, but it does not state that a client receives or can verify those proofs, so no client-verifiable mechanism is documented.

upstream_disclosure.note: The terms state what the operator's servers see: "In standard API mode, our servers may transiently read your request in memory to process it (e.g., extracting the model name for routing, or fetching images for vision models), but this data is never written to any database, log, or persistent storage." The security-architecture page states the compute is provided by anonymous, permissionless miners inside trusted execution environments.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Chutes terms of service, for Chutes

credential_handling.note: The API offers no customer-supplied-key path: the authentication page documents Chutes-issued keys ("Use the key as a bearer token.") and OAuth sign-in only.

cache_isolation.note: No prompt or prefix caching scope is documented on the security-architecture page or elsewhere in the documentation.

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The contact page publishes a security route: "Security Report vulnerabilities or security concerns. support@chutes.ai".

independent_audit.note: No SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent attestation is named on the security-architecture page or elsewhere.
